content.introduction: The United States indicators show a mixed economic picture as of September 2026. Industrial Production increased by 0.7% month-over-month, while Manufacturing Production rose by 1.1%. Capacity Utilization stood at 76.9%, up from 76.4% the previous month. Durable Goods Orders were flat in August, but Durable Goods Orders Ex Defense and Ex Transportation saw slight increases. The Conference Board Coincident Economic Index® (CEI) increased by 0.3% in September to 115.3 (2016=100), following a 0.1% rise in August. The CEI has risen by 0.9% over the six months between March and September 2026. The unemployment rate was 4.2% in September, and Non Farm Payrolls increased by 29 thousand.

The Conference Board Coincident Economic Index® (CEI) for the US increased by 0.3% in September 2026 to 115.3 (2016=100), following a 0.1% increase in August. Overall, the CEI rose by 0.9% over the six months between March and September 2026, up from its 0.2% growth over the previous six months. About The Conference Board _Leading Economic Index®_(LEI) and _Coincident Economic Index®_(CEI) for the US  
 The composite economic indexes are key elements in an analytic system designed to signal peaks and troughs in the business cycle. Comprised of multiple independent indicators, the indexes are constructed to summarize and reveal common turning points in the economy in a clearer and more convincing manner than any individual component.
